### Summary

Workspace Cloud SDK arguments could execute code during Gmail setup. In affected versions, an untrusted workspace `.env` could set `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_ARGS`. Gmail setup inherited that value when starting `gcloud`, whose launcher passed it as arguments to Python.

This advisory is scoped to operators who started OpenClaw in attacker-controlled workspace content and then invoked the Gmail setup flow.

### Impact

A crafted `CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_ARGS` value could make the trusted Python interpreter execute attacker-supplied code when Gmail setup ran `gcloud`. The code ran with the OpenClaw host user's permissions and could read credentials, modify files, or start other processes.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.8.1`.

### Mitigations

Upgrade to `openclaw@2026.8.1` or later. Before upgrading, run Gmail setup only from trusted workspaces and clear inherited `CLOUDSDK_*` variables before invoking it.
